question: Can bounded payment retries rescue reserved buyers without displacing new buyers, and can server scheduling improve the tradeoff?
correctness: Apply sticky terminal review and exact KRW validation equally before all new measurements. Old measurements remain historical.
old_15_percent_rule: Applied to the prior budget-boundary adoption decision only. It is not a permanent exclusion of late-budget and is not this experiment's criterion.

client_policy.name: closed-only-3
client_policy.trigger: Explicit HTTP 503 with code PAYMENT_ADMISSION_CLOSED only
client_policy.jitter: Multiply each delay by 0.8 + hash(index, seed + 0x6000 + retryNumber*7919)%401 / 1000. Independent of user/action/PG streams.
client_policy.identity: Reuse reservation, paymentKey, orderId, amount, currency and original Idempotency-Key. Never creates a new logical user/opportunity.
client_policy.stop: Stop on any non-CLOSED response, accepted payment, attempt cap, or 10s since logical start. Each call is capped by remaining deadline. Original reservation expiry is unchanged; measured HOLD_SECONDS=15 exceeds the 10s logical deadline.
client_policy.ambiguous_response: Do not treat transport failure or generic 503 as an empty transaction. Bounded reservation GET and durable server recovery; no new identity/key. Record ambiguous response separately.
client_policy.control: One physical payment attempt with identical input seed, PG faults, API timeout bound and status observation policy. All retry calls and observer CPU are counted.

measurement.pilot: Independent 100/400 per base with once/closed-only-3, warm5s@10, measure25s; 10s per-target deadline; same repeat seed61001. Classify client effects before selecting server hypothesis.
measurement.final: Freeze executable, harness, config, seed. Independent warm20s@10 + gap5 + measure90s. 100/400, 3 repetitions, same seeds61001..61003. Sequential shared-host runs, alternate ordering. Includes both bases with identical retry policy and one-shot controls.
measurement.resources: DB2CPU/1GiB, JVM384MiB ActiveProcessorCount2 hint, pool48, worker4, pending256, admission24, HTTP2048, scheduler2, inbox100000. No capacity enlargement as improvement.
measurement.stock: 2,000,000 for bottleneck; separate finite-stock workload, fixed capacity/demand declared before that comparison. No actual PG synthetic load.
outcomes: first CLOSED then retry accepted and purchased by 10s
additional physical payment API calls and DB cost
first-attempt acceptance and first-attempt-purchased rates over all planned payment targets, plus conditional denominators
first-call and successful first/retry purchase latency
wall-window purchase commits including older arrivals
whole-host CPU with same-window purchase denominator

client_adoption.gate: All correctness and final convergence; no generator dropped iterations
client_adoption.400: Mean total deadline purchases >=3% relative above matched one-shot and positive paired net in >=2/3 repetitions. First-attempt-purchased share of all targets may not fall by more than 2 percentage points.
client_adoption.100: Deadline purchase rate drop <=1 percentage point
client_adoption.cost: Whole-host CPU per purchase <=1.15 times matched one-shot. First payment-call p95 <=1.25 times control.

server_adoption.reference: Compare to BOTH corrected pull and corrected late under the same bounded retry policy; compare full user outcome also to both one-shot arms.
server_adoption.gate: All correctness, no class starvation in deterministic mixed-ready test, global pending bound unchanged, drain<=600s, no generator drops
server_adoption.400: Mean deadline purchases >=3% relative above the stronger retry reference and positive paired net in >=2/3 repeats against that reference. First-attempt-purchased share may not drop >2pp versus either retry reference.
server_adoption.100: Deadline purchase rate no more than 1pp worse than either retry reference
server_adoption.cost: CPU per purchase <=1.10 times the lower-cost retry reference; successful p99 and expiry-return p99 <=1.20 times the stronger-outcome retry reference. Report absolute CPU and all failures even if gates pass.
server_adoption.fallback: If new candidate fails, retain the best qualifying existing structure/policy by total deadline buyers, first-customer protection and CPU. Differences below3% without consistent paired gain are inconclusive; prefer lower cost then simpler structure. Do not retrofit thresholds after observing results.
